questions.text:
Consider the following minterm expression for F.
F(P,Q,R,S) = [latex]\Sigma[/latex] 0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15
The minterms 2, 7, 8 and 13 are 'do not care terms. The minimal sum of-products form for F is
questions.solution:
Minterms 0, 5, 10, 15 with don't cares 2, 7, 8, 13.

- [latex]\bar Q\bar S[/latex] = {0, 2, 8, 10} covers 0, 10
- [latex]QS[/latex] = {5, 7, 13, 15} covers 5, 15

[latex]F=\bar Q\bar S+QS[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\bar Q\bar S+QS[/latex]

questions.text:
The value of a float type variable is represented using the single-precision 32-bit floating
point format of IEEE-754 standard that uses 1 bit for sign, 8 bits for biased exponent and 23
bits for mantissa. A float type variable x is assigned the decimal value of -14.25. The
representation of x in hexadecimal notation is
questions.solution:
[latex]14.25=(1110.01)_2=1.11001\times2^3[/latex]

- Sign = 1
- Exponent = 3 + 127 = 130 = 10000010
- Mantissa = 1100100...0

1 10000010 11001000... = 1100 0001 0110 0100 0000... = C1640000H

Answer: C1640000H

questions.text:
Consider the equation [latex](123)_{5}=(x8)_{y}[/latex]  with x and y as unknown. The number of possible
solutions is _____ .
questions.solution:
[latex](123)_5=25+10+3=38[/latex]
[latex](x8)_y=xy+8=38\Rightarrow xy=30[/latex], with digit 8 needing [latex]y\gt 8[/latex] and [latex]1\le x\lt y[/latex].

Factor pairs of 30: (x, y) = (3, 10), (2, 15), (1, 30).

Answer: 3

questions.text: Let  [latex]k = 2^{n}[/latex] . A circuit is built by giving the output of an n-bit binary counter as input to an n-to-[latex]2^{n}[/latex] bit decoder. This circuit is equivalent to a
questions.solution:
The n-bit counter goes 0, 1, 2, ..., [latex]2^n-1[/latex]. The decoder makes exactly one of its [latex]k=2^n[/latex] outputs 1 for each count.

So the single 1 moves 000..1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 00..10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ... [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10..0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] back to start. This is exactly a k-bit ring counter.

Answer: k-bit ring counter
